title: Replace wall-clock DateTime.now() with fixed UTC literals in learning-repository test fixtures
why: These three files read the real system clock (not even .toUtc()) to satisfy required timestamp columns, while sibling files in the same batch (completion_repository_curriculum_dedup_test.dart, completion_writer_test.dart, learning_ledger_repository_impl_test.dart) consistently use DateTime.now().toUtc() or fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals -- an inconsistent idiom that Rule 0's own check 6/15 ('No DateTime.now() outside core/time') explicitly cannot catch because it scopes only to lib/ and excludes test/ entirely.
recommendation: Replace the bare DateTime.now() calls with fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals for these non-asserted fixture columns, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the same batch.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'DateTime\.now()' test/features/learning --include='*.dart' returns no hits outside intentionally wall-clock-dependent assertions
